bear.text: Direct cousin of invalidated DON-20/10-ATR: same donchian_breakout system, same entry=20/exit=10 parameters. That strategy was invalidated (OOS Sharpe 0.87, maxDD -40.2%) not because the parameters were wrong but because the OOS drawdown was untradable. In-sample Sharpe 0.81 here does not distinguish this idea from its invalidated cousin — only OOS behavior can.

In-sample Sharpe 0.81 trails SPY buy-and-hold (~0.9) over the same window. The Tier-1 'beat benchmark net' gate is the binding constraint: a trend system on SPY that cannot beat holding SPY is complexity without compensation.

Round 3 screened 70 combinations, so the Tier-1 DSR uses n_trials=70. At n=70 the expected best Sharpe under the null is roughly 0.9-1.0; an in-sample 0.81 is unlikely to clear DSR > 0.8. The research-bar score does not deflate for the round's multiplicity — the DSR will.

Backtest uses fixed-quantity sizing (100 shares): notional drifts with price, so the Sharpe mixes different risk budgets across the 11-year sample. Screening-grade only — any trial must use volatility-normalized sizing.

bull.text: 52 trades over 11 years with in-sample maxDD only 4.1%: the profile of a persistent small edge, not a lucky tail bet. Score 0.75 is the highest in the round.

evidence.value: trend persistence in index ETF flows

bull.text: Economic rationale exists: Donchian breakouts on SPY harvest the well-documented slow diffusion of macro news into index prices. Not a mined pattern — a risk-premium-adjacent phenomenon.

evidence.value: WF OOS Sharpe > 0.3 and DSR > 0.8 at n=70

bull.text: The cousinship objection is testable, not fatal: if walk-forward OOS Sharpe clears 0.3 with DSR > 0.8 at the full round multiplicity, this idea has earned separation from DON-20/10-ATR. The trial-4 amendment precedent shows the lane records both verdicts honestly.

bear.text: Cousin of invalidated TREND-VT (trend on equities, OOS Sharpe 0.09 in trial 3). The lane's trend experiments keep dying out-of-sample: DON-20/10-ATR on drawdown, TREND-VT on Sharpe. SMA(10,30) on SPY must explain why it is different, not just smoother in-sample.
In-sample Sharpe 0.73 trails SPY buy-and-hold (~0.9) over the same window. A moving-average crossover that underperforms buy-and-hold in its own discovery sample faces a steep Tier-1 benchmark gate.
At n_trials=70, DSR > 0.8 needs Sharpe_hat far above the null's expected best (~0.9-1.0). In-sample 0.73 is below that bar before walk-forward even begins. Statistically, this idea starts underwater.
43 trades in 11 years (~4/yr): each trade carries enormous weight in the Sharpe estimate. One missed 2020 rebound trade in OOS and the edge halves.

bull.text: MaxDD 6.6% in-sample with 43 trades: the SMA(10,30) stayed invested through trends and stepped aside in chop. The drawdown profile is what a trend system should look like.
Score 0.63 clears the 0.30 research bar by 2x. The desk's bar already penalizes thin evidence via the trade_factor ramp — this idea earned its place.

evidence.value: beats SPY net in OOS folds

bull.text: If the walk-forward shows positive excess vs SPY net of costs across folds, the benchmark objection dissolves — the strategy would have beaten buy-and-hold where it counts: unseen data.

evidence.value: same scout, same symbol, same strategy family as idea 1

bear.text: Same scout, same symbol (SPY), same strategy family as idea 1 — SMA(20,50) vs SMA(10,30). These are not two independent ideas; they are two parameter draws from one idea. Counting both toward n_screened is honest, but promoting both would double-count one phenomenon.
Only 25 trades in 11 years (~2/yr) with maxDD 10.7% — the highest drawdown among the trend ideas. Slow systems concentrate risk in few decisions; the Sharpe 0.72 rests on a thin decision base.
Same DSR arithmetic as idea 1, worse: in-sample 0.72 at n=70. The null's expected best Sharpe at 70 trials sits above this idea's point estimate.
Trails SPY buy-and-hold (~0.9) in-sample. A slower, choppier version of idea 1 with no compensating advantage.

bull.text: SMA(20,50) is the slower sibling: fewer whipsaws, longer holds, different return profile than idea 1. If the desk wants trend exposure, the parameter-diversified pair is more robust than either alone.
Thin but testable: 25 trades is enough for a walk-forward verdict. If OOS Sharpe clears 0.3 the idea survives on its own merits; if not, it was the weaker sibling all along.

evidence.params: donchian entry=20 exit=10 on single name

bear.text: Same donchian 20/10 system as invalidated DON-20/10-ATR, now on AAPL instead of its original universe. Changing the symbol is not a new thesis — it is the same system auditioning on a friendlier stage. AAPL's 2015-2026 run flatters every trend system.

Secular contamination flag: AAPL rose roughly 10x over the sample. Any long-biased trend system prints a positive Sharpe on a 10x underlying. The edge must be measured against buy-and-hold AAPL, not against zero.

In-sample maxDD of 4.4% on a single stock over 11 years including 2020 and 2022 is suspiciously clean — it suggests the system sat out the crashes by luck of timing, a property that rarely repeats OOS. Expect OOS drawdowns an order of magnitude larger, as DON-20/10-ATR demonstrated (-40.2%).

bull.text: 44 trades, Sharpe 0.63, DD 4.4%: consistent with the SPY donchian idea (idea 0), suggesting the donchian phenomenon is not symbol-specific — the very parameter-consistency the desk looks for.

evidence.value: excess vs AAPL buy-and-hold net > 0 OOS

bull.text: The benchmark objection has a clean test: excess return vs AAPL buy-and-hold, net of costs, in OOS folds. If positive, the system adds value beyond riding the secular wave.

bear.text: Supertrend is an ATR-trailing trend system — cousin of both DON-20/10-ATR (ATR exits) and TREND-VT (invalidated trial 3). The lane has now invalidated ATR-based trend twice. A third needs exceptional OOS evidence, not in-sample 0.58.
Same secular-contamination flag as idea 3: MSFT's multi-year cloud run flatters long-biased trend. The 7.3% in-sample maxDD will not survive contact with a real single-name drawdown.
In-sample Sharpe 0.58 is the weakest of the trend ideas and sits far below the n=70 null expectation (~0.9-1.0). DSR > 0.8 is a long shot arithmetically.

bull.text: 42 trades with the lowest score in the family (0.47) — but it still cleared the bar, and Supertrend's ATR trailing stop is structurally different from Donchian's fixed exit: it adapts position to volatility rather than time.
Weakest bull case in the round; the honest verdict is to let the walk-forward decide quickly. If OOS Sharpe < 0.3, discard without ceremony — the family already has stronger candidates.

bear.text: In-sample Sharpe 0.53 on JPM bollinger reversion. Short-term mean reversion on daily bars is among the most published anomalies in equities; a 0.53 in-sample Sharpe after the desk's own selection is weak evidence of a surviving edge — the publication decay on daily MR is well documented.

55 trades over 11 years (~5/yr) for a 'short-term' mean-reversion system is slow — true short-term MR trades weekly or more. The holding periods here bleed into swing territory, where the MR rationale (overnight reversal, bid-ask bounce) no longer applies.

Same DSR arithmetic as the trend ideas: 0.53 in-sample at n=70 is far below the null's expected best. The DSR gate will almost surely fail — and that is the gate doing its job against a mined MR parameter.

JPM buy-and-hold over 2015-2026 was strong (banks' post-2016 run). The Tier-1 benchmark gate needs excess vs holding JPM — a mean-reversion system that underperforms its own underlying's drift is a hard sell.

bull.text: MaxDD 3.9% — the tightest drawdown in the round. Whatever this system is capturing on JPM, it does so with minimal pain, which is exactly the profile the Tier-1 maxDD gate rewards.

evidence.value: daily equity MR vs MR-5M (5-min crypto)

bull.text: Not a direct cousin of invalidated MR-5M: different timeframe (daily vs 5-minute), different asset class (bank equity vs crypto), different cost structure. The invalidation does not transfer automatically.

Daily timeframe on JPM (deep liquidity): 5 bps/side is conservative and the cost-sensitivity curve should be flat. Unlike MR-5M, costs are unlikely to be the executioner here — the verdict will come from the DSR and benchmark gates instead.

evidence.value: Connors RSI(2) — most mined short-term MR system in existence

bear.text: RSI(2) on SPY is the single most mined short-term mean-reversion system in the literature (Connors). An in-sample Sharpe of 0.49 on the most studied MR setup in existence, after the desk screened 70 combos, is the textbook profile of a decayed-and-mined edge. Publication decay is the prior; the data must overcome it.

92 trades sounds like evidence, but over 11 years it is ~8/yr — and RSI(2) signals cluster in stress episodes (2020, 2022). The Sharpe likely rides a handful of crash-rebound trades. Remove March 2020 and re-examine.
In-sample 0.49 at n=70: the DSR will fail. The null's expected best-of-70 Sharpe sits near 1.0; 0.49 does not survive deflation no matter how the folds look.
Trails SPY buy-and-hold (~0.9) by a wide margin in-sample. A mean-reversion system on SPY that cannot beat holding SPY, in its own discovery sample, has no Tier-1 path.

bull.text: 92 trades is the deepest evidence base in the round, and maxDD 3.6% is contained. If any MR idea deserves the walk-forward, it is the one with the most decisions behind it.

Concentration in stress episodes cuts both ways: a system that buys SPY panic and survives is providing liquidity when it is scarcest — a genuine economic function, and the worst-regime lens of the old gate set would have rewarded exactly this.

The crash-dependence objection is testable: walk-forward OOS Sharpe excluding the 2020 episode. If the edge survives ex-2020, it is broader than one rebound; if not, discard — the idea was March 2020 in a trench coat.

evidence.value: same strategy+params as idea 5 (bollinger 20/2.0), different symbol

bear.text: Same bollinger_reversion(20, 2.0) system as idea 5, on MSFT instead of JPM. One parameter draw, two symbols — not two independent ideas. If bollinger MR is real it should work across symbols, but the two instances must not be double-counted as separate discoveries.
MSFT's secular run contaminates the long-biased MR: buying dips in a 8x uptrend prints money in-sample. The benchmark gate (excess vs MSFT buy-and-hold) is the honest judge.
In-sample 0.51 at n=70 — same DSR arithmetic as idea 5. Fails the deflation test before walk-forward.

evidence.value: bollinger MR clears bar on JPM and MSFT

bull.text: The same (20, 2.0) parameters clear the research bar on two different symbols (JPM, MSFT) — parameter robustness across names is evidence against overfitting to one price path.
MaxDD 5.4% on a single name with 49 trades: contained. If the walk-forward confirms, this is the diversifying complement to the trend ideas — MR and trend are natural portfolio partners at Tier-2.

evidence.value: excess vs MSFT buy-and-hold net > 0 OOS

bull.text: Clean falsifier: excess vs MSFT buy-and-hold net of costs in OOS folds. Positive means the system adds value beyond the secular drift; negative means it was surfing.

evidence.value: third instance of bollinger_reversion(20,2.0): JPM, MSFT, now SPY

bear.text: Third instance of the identical bollinger(20, 2.0) system — JPM, MSFT, now SPY. The desk has discovered one idea three times. Sharpe 0.50, DD 7.9%: the weakest of the three instances, and SPY is the symbol where the trend scout also found ideas — the desk is now long/short-ambiguous on the same underlying.
MaxDD 7.9% is the deepest among the MR ideas despite SPY being the most diversified underlying — the system held losers longer here. Drawdown discipline is worse where it should be best.
In-sample 0.50 at n=70. Same DSR verdict as its siblings.

bull.text: Three-for-three across JPM/MSFT/SPY with identical parameters is the strongest cross-sectional consistency in the round. If this is mining, it is mining the same vein in three places — which is what a real vein looks like.
Weakest of the three siblings; rank it third in any trial queue. Its value is confirmatory, not standalone.

bear.text: Z-score(20, entry 2.0) reversion is bollinger(20, 2.0) reversion in different notation — same 2-sigma fade logic on SPY. The desk has now found the same idea four times (ideas 5, 7, 8, 9). The round's '15 ideas' are closer to 10 distinct phenomena, and the MR cluster is one of them.
MaxDD 8.3%, deepest of the MR cluster on the most diversified underlying. The z-score variant held losers longest — variant inferiority, not diversification.
In-sample 0.50 at n=70. DSR fails.

bull.text: 59 trades, consistent with its siblings. Its only bull case is as a robustness check on the bollinger/zscore MR phenomenon — a confirming witness, not a candidate.
Rank fourth among the MR siblings. Do not trial independently; fold into a family-level verdict.

bear.text: 14 trades in 11 years. The standard error on a Sharpe estimated from 14 trades is enormous — roughly 0.27 per unit Sharpe, so the 0.60 point estimate is statistically indistinguishable from zero. The desk's trade_factor ramp (n/10 capped at 1.0) stops penalizing after 10 trades, which is far too generous for a 14-trade idea to score 0.48.

Bollinger-squeeze with a 60-day squeeze lookback is a two-knob system (period, lookback) selected from a 70-combo sweep. With 14 trades, the lookback knob can easily be fit to the sample's volatility episodes. This is the highest selection-risk idea in the round.
In-sample 0.60 on 14 trades at n=70: the DSR has nothing to work with. Deflated Sharpe will be near zero — correctly.
MaxDD 8.1% on 14 trades means individual trades carried large losses — the return distribution is lumpy, and the Sortino gate will punish the downside lumps.

bull.text: Structurally the most distinct niche in the round: volatility-compression-then-expansion is a different return generator than trend or MR, with a genuine economic story (options-hedging flows amplify post-squeeze moves). Long-vol-friendly profile.

The honest path: this idea needs more evidence, not more argument. A longer sample or a confirming sibling (idea 14 on AAPL is the start) — otherwise discard on thin evidence regardless of the point estimate.
Even the bull case concedes: 14 trades cannot carry a Tier-1 verdict. Rank as 'interesting phenomenon, insufficient evidence' — a watchlist item, not a candidate.

evidence.value: keltner_breakout = ATR-channel trend breakout; cousin of donchian_breakout

bear.text: Keltner breakout is an ATR-channel breakout — a trend-breakout cousin wearing volatility clothing. The lane invalidated donchian-breakout trend (DON-20/10-ATR) and vol-targeted trend (TREND-VT). The 'volatility' label does not make this a new family; it is the trend family with an ATR envelope.
AAPL's secular 10x run flatters every long-biased breakout system. Same contamination flag as idea 3 — the benchmark gate vs AAPL buy-and-hold is binding.
In-sample 0.53 at n=70. Below the null's expected best; DSR fails.

evidence.value: identical params on AAPL/NVDA/SPY = 1 idea tested 3x

bear.text: Identical {ema 20, atr 10, mult 2.0} on three symbols: this is one idea with three observations, and the round's n_screened=70 already counts the multiplicity honestly. Do not treat ideas 11/12/13 as three independent discoveries.

evidence.value: same params clear bar on AAPL, NVDA, SPY

bull.text: The identical parameter set clears the research bar on three different underlyings (AAPL, NVDA, SPY) — the strongest parameter-robustness signal in the round. Mined parameters do not usually survive the symbol transfer; these did.
48 trades with maxDD 4.5%: solid evidence base, contained pain. Among the vol-breakout ideas this is the workhorse.

evidence.value: excess vs AAPL buy-and-hold net > 0 OOS

bull.text: If the walk-forward shows positive excess vs AAPL buy-and-hold net of costs, the secular-contamination objection is answered and the cross-symbol consistency becomes a genuine phenomenon worth trialing.

bear.text: NVDA's 2023-2024 AI melt-up (roughly 10x in under two years) dominates the sample window. A breakout system that was long NVDA through 2023-2024 prints Sharpe 0.48 on that episode alone. The question is not whether the system caught the melt-up — it is whether it has any edge outside it. Walk-forward folds excluding 2023-2024 are the test.

evidence.value: same params as ideas 11/13; trend-breakout family

bear.text: Third instance of the identical keltner parameters; trend-breakout family. Its fate should be decided at the family level with ideas 11 and 13, not as a standalone.
In-sample 0.48 at n=70 — the weakest in-sample Sharpe among the keltner trio. DSR fails.

bull.text: Part of the cross-symbol-consistent keltner trio. Its standalone case is weak, but as a confirming observation it strengthens the family's claim — if the family survives OOS ex-NVDA-melt-up.
The melt-up exclusion test is decisive: OOS Sharpe above 0.3 excluding 2023-2024 keeps it alive as a family member; below, and it was the AI run in a trench coat.

evidence.value: keltner on SPY; trend scout already has 3 SPY trend ideas

bear.text: Keltner breakout on SPY joins ideas 0, 1, 2 (donchian/SMA trend on SPY) — the desk now has four trend-breakout ideas on the same underlying. At the portfolio level these are one correlated bet; Tier-2 diversification math would collapse them. The marginal value of a fourth SPY trend system is near zero.
In-sample Sharpe 0.45 is the weakest in the round and trails SPY buy-and-hold (~0.9) by half. The benchmark gate is out of reach.
In-sample 0.45 at n=70. DSR fails by the widest margin in the round.

bull.text: 50 trades, maxDD 4.1% — the evidence base is real and the pain is contained. As the SPY representative of the keltner family it is the cleanest test case (no single-name secular contamination).
No standalone bull case — its fate belongs to the keltner family's OOS verdict. If the family clears Tier-1, the SPY instance is the trial vehicle; if not, discard with the family.

bear.text: 15 trades — same thin-evidence objection as idea 10. A Sharpe of 0.47 on 15 trades is noise with a point estimate. The squeeze lookback (60 days) is a second fitted knob on a 15-observation base.
Second instance of the squeeze system (idea 10 on QQQ). Two thin-evidence instances do not sum to one solid idea — 14 + 15 trades across different symbols is still a small, heterogeneous base.
In-sample 0.47 at n=70. DSR fails.

evidence.value: squeeze clears bar on QQQ and AAPL

bull.text: The squeeze phenomenon clears the bar on two symbols (QQQ, AAPL) with the same parameters — a confirming witness for idea 10. The phenomenon is interesting; the evidence base is not yet sufficient.
Watchlist, not candidate: the squeeze family needs a longer sample or an intraday variant with more trades before it can face Tier-1 honestly.
